ai-at-work.title: Sam Altman says people need to accept ‘some bad things’ are going to happen if they want AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: OpenAI Group PBC Chief Executive Sam Altman insists that the security risks of artificial intelligence need to be taken seriously. But unlike his counterpart Dario Amodei of Anthropic PBC, he believes
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Sam Altman is basically saying we need to accept collateral damage as the price of AI progress. For digital workplace leaders, this is the moment to stop waiting for perfect AI governance and start building your own guardrails now, because apparently safety is something you negotiate later. It's like OpenAI's saying "trust us, it'll probably be fine" while you're supposed to implement this thing in your company tomorrow.

ai-at-work.title: Trump launches Super Intelligence Force with Jay Clayton as AI czar
ai-at-work.excerpt: President Donald Trump today put Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton in charge of a new federal artificial intelligence task force, making him the administration’s second AI czar. Trump reve
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Trump has appointed Jay Clayton, the Director of National Intelligence, to lead a new federal AI task force called the "Super Intelligence Force," making him the second AI czar in this administration. This matters to digital workplace pros because government AI policy directly shapes what enterprise tools get approved, funded, and mandated across corporate America. Honestly, if we're on our second AI czar before anyone's figured out what the first one was supposed to do, that tells you everything you need to know about how seriously Washington takes actual digital strategy.

ai-at-work.excerpt: Agentic artificial intelligence is changing the identity security equation. Enterprises are no longer governing access only for employees and traditional machine identities. AI agents can act on behal
ai-at-work.dwp_take: SailPoint is hosting its Navigate event October 6-7 to dig into how agentic AI is reshaping identity and access management, since AI agents now request and use permissions just like humans do. This matters to digital workplace pros because managing access just got exponentially more complex: your governance frameworks now need to handle autonomous AI actors alongside traditional users and systems. Here's the honest truth: if your current identity strategy still treats access as a human problem, you're already behind, and SailPoint knows it.

ai-at-work.title: Robotics AI developer FieldAI reportedly raising $700M in funding
ai-at-work.excerpt: FieldAI Inc., a startup that develops artificial intelligence models for robots, is reportedly seeking $700 million in funding. A source told Business Insider today that the round could value the comp
ai-at-work.dwp_take: FieldAI, a robotics AI startup, is raising $700 million at a $10 billion valuation, up from $2 billion just months earlier. This matters because AI-powered automation is creeping into workplace operations, from document processing to facilities management, and digital workplace leaders need to understand how these tools will reshape their infrastructure and workforce planning. The valuation jump is either a sign of genuine breakthrough technology or a reminder that not every AI company throwing around billions will actually solve your real workplace problems.

industry-news.title: AMD Launches Ross AI Assistant for Embedded Development
industry-news.excerpt: AMD Ross helps engineers design, optimize, and debug embedded systems. Learn about supported tools, licensing requirements, and deployment options. The post AMD Launches Ross AI Assistant for Embedded
industry-news.dwp_take: AMD just released Ross, an AI assistant specifically built to help engineers with embedded system design, optimization, and debugging work. This matters because digital workplace teams managing technical infrastructure and developer tools now have another AI option to evaluate for improving engineering productivity and reducing time spent on routine troubleshooting tasks. Honestly though, we've got so many AI assistants launching these days that the real question isn't whether Ross exists, it's whether your engineers will actually use it or just stick with whatever they already know.

industry-news.title: Windows 11 26H2 Update: Which PCs Get the Enablement Package
industry-news.excerpt: Windows 11 26H2 brings a fast enablement-package upgrade to 24H2 and 25H2 PCs, while 26H1 devices remain on a separate path. The post Windows 11 26H2 Update: Which PCs Get the Enablement Package appea
industry-news.dwp_take: Microsoft released Windows 11 26H2 as an enablement package that updates certain PC versions while leaving others on their own upgrade path. This matters because it creates yet another fragmentation layer in your fleet management, meaning your IT team now needs to track which devices get which version and when they'll actually get it. After three decades watching Microsoft's versioning strategy, I can confirm this is basically them playing 4D chess while the rest of us are still figuring out checkers.

industry-news.title: Snowflake urges companies to embrace the era of the agentic enterprise
industry-news.excerpt: The pace of change is unrelenting, so doing nothing is no longer an option, the AI data firm told attendees at a recent event in London…
industry-news.dwp_take: Snowflake is telling companies they need to get serious about AI agents handling enterprise tasks or risk getting left behind. This matters to digital workplace folks because autonomous agents are going to fundamentally change how work gets done, who does it, and what skills actually matter in an office. Here's the thing though: every vendor says "embrace change or die," and most companies are still struggling with basic collaboration tools, so maybe pump the brakes on the existential dread and focus on getting your fundamentals right first.

industry-news.title: NetApp Insight 2026: Can Novus and Keystone break the AI bottlenecks?
industry-news.excerpt: We're back in Vegas as Ross Kelly talks us through all the news from NetApp Insight 2026
industry-news.dwp_take: NetApp announced Novus and Keystone at their Vegas conference, positioning both as solutions to tackle AI infrastructure bottlenecks that are currently slowing down enterprise deployments. This matters because data storage and management remain the unsexy but critical foundation that every AI initiative actually needs to function, and most organizations are still struggling with this unglamorous reality. Look, if your AI strategy falls apart because your storage can't keep up, all those fancy LLM conversations don't mean much, so NetApp is at least tackling the real problem instead of just selling you another chatbot.
